gaps.sentence: I ___ dinner when the lights went out.
gaps.hint: the lights went out interrupted it
gaps.explanation: The lights going out interrupted an ongoing background action, so the past continuous is used: was cooking.

gaps.sentence: The soup ___ delicious, but I think it needs a little more salt.
gaps.hint: taste describing a quality is stative
gaps.explanation: When 'taste' describes a quality of something, it is a state verb: tastes.

gaps.sentence: When I was a boy, films ___ in black and white.
gaps.hint: a past state no longer existing
gaps.explanation: 'Used to be' describes a past state that has ended: used to be.

gaps.sentence: I usually walk to work, but today I ___ the bus because it is raining.
gaps.hint: today contrasts with the usual habit
gaps.explanation: 'But today' signals a temporary break from habit, so the present continuous is correct: am taking.

gaps.sentence: The conference ___ on Monday and ends on Wednesday.
gaps.explanation: Fixed schedules are stated in the present simple: starts.

gaps.sentence: Shakespeare ___ thirty-seven plays that we know of.
gaps.hint: a dead historical figure, finished lifetime
gaps.explanation: Actions of people who are no longer alive take the past simple even without a time phrase: wrote.

gaps.sentence: This time next week I ___ across the desert.
gaps.hint: action in progress at a future time
gaps.explanation: 'This time next week' — future continuous for an ongoing future action.

gaps.sentence: By Friday, the climbers ___ on the north face for six days without a break.
gaps.hint: duration measured to a future point
gaps.explanation: 'By Friday + for six days' calls for the future perfect: will have been.
